issues.finding: M6 scan_codex_via_mapping uses inline python3 -c with single-quoted bash; the map_file path is interpolated via shell expansion ($map_file inside the python source). If a daemon-home path ever contains a single quote, the python source would be malformed. Not a security issue (HAPPY_HOMES is admin-controlled) but a quoting fragility worth fixing on user-side application.
issues.recommendation: Pass map_file as an argv (sys.argv[1]) rather than interpolated string literal: python3 -c 'import sys,json,os; ...' "$map_file"

code_quality_findings.issue: BA spec AC3 explicitly said 'Use a mocked fs module to assert each step fires in order.' Dev substituted observable-filesystem-state verification with note 'ESM disallows vi.spyOn on fs/promises'. The substitution is reasonable given Node ESM limitations, and the source code (atomicWriteJson.ts) implements the documented sequence verbatim (writeAndSyncTmp → rename → fsyncDir). Codex confirmed the substitution does not materially weaken the atomicity contract; only fsync-order-regression would not be auto-caught beyond code review.
code_quality_findings.recommendation: Acceptable as-is for this cycle. Future: consider migrating atomicWriteJson to dependency-injected fs (or a higher-level wrapper) so unit tests CAN spy on individual syscalls. File this as dimension=spec_text_vs_execution_drift in BA ledger so future cycles use the actually-runnable formulation.
